name: Nightfall Schism

detectability.signature: Jagged linear tear emitting radiation on frequencies that do not correspond to any known electromagnetic spectrum; gravimetric sensors detect mass readings that oscillate between positive and negative values

proximity: Navigation instruments give contradictory readings, simultaneously reporting multiple incompatible spatial coordinates
Visible light from the rift shifts through colors not normally perceptible to human vision
Hull-mounted cameras capture imagery of structures and landscapes that have no corresponding physical source
contact: Partial or complete translocation into an adjacent dimensional space with unknown physical laws
Matter in contact with the rift edge undergoes molecular reconfiguration into unknown crystalline structures
Ship systems receive data streams from sensors that do not exist on the vessel
prolonged_exposure: Crew experience overlapping perceptions of two realities, leading to severe cognitive dissonance
Ship materials begin exhibiting properties inconsistent with their molecular composition
Localized physics anomalies manifest aboard: gravity reversals, spontaneous temperature inversions, light bending at impossible angles

age: Unknown; first detected approximately 200 years ago, but stellar scarring suggests periodic appearances over millennia

behavior.cycle: The rift widens by approximately 3 kilometers per decade, with periodic contractions lasting weeks to months

phenomena: The rift itself appears as a jagged tear in space, its edges limned with light that shifts through impossible colors — hues that exist outside the visible spectrum yet are somehow perceived
Through the rift, observers report seeing vast alien geometries: cities of black glass, skies with multiple horizons, landscapes that fold upward into themselves
Objects near the rift occasionally develop mirror-image duplicates that persist for seconds to hours before dissolving
Electromagnetic transmissions passing near the rift are returned with additional data appended — messages in no known language or encoding
hazards: The rift edge restructures matter on contact, making even incidental physical intersection with the boundary lethal to vessels
Expanding boundary makes long-term safe-distance calculations unreliable
Cognitive effects on crew from prolonged visual observation can produce permanent perceptual disorders
opportunities: The rift offers potential access to alternate dimensional spaces with unknown resources and physics
Crystalline structures formed at the rift edge exhibit material properties unachievable through conventional manufacturing
Data streams received from beyond the rift may contain information from an entirely foreign knowledge base
known_incidents: In 2438, the research cruiser Eventide launched a purpose-built probe into the Nightfall Schism; the probe transmitted 4.7 seconds of data before signal loss, including imagery of a vast dark ocean beneath a sky containing no stars, only a single luminous band of deep violet stretching from horizon to horizon

Three ships of the Marchetti Salvage Cooperative strayed within 500 kilometers of the rift edge in 2461 while pursuing a debris field; one vessel, the Corrival, was partially intersected by an erratic expansion of the boundary, and the severed portion was never recovered — the remaining hull section showed a perfectly smooth cross-section of crystallized metal at the cut
description: The Nightfall Schism presents as a ragged laceration in the fabric of three-dimensional space, a wound roughly 24,000 kilometers across at its widest and shaped like a torn curtain. Its edges blaze with light in colors that defy classification, shifting through spectral ranges that human eyes should not be able to perceive yet somehow do. Through the tear, the darkness beyond is not empty — it is filled with alien geometries, vast and terrible structures that obey no recognizable physical law.

The Schism's behavior is deeply troubling to researchers. It is expanding, slowly but measurably, widening by roughly three kilometers each decade. Periodic contractions offer temporary respite, but the overall trend is growth. Ships approaching within several thousand kilometers report navigational instruments producing contradictory readings, as though the vessel exists in two spatial frameworks simultaneously. Visual observation of the rift interior produces lasting psychological effects in a significant percentage of viewers.

First detected two centuries ago by a long-range survey array, the Nightfall Schism's origins remain completely unknown. Geological analysis of nearby stellar bodies shows periodic scarring patterns consistent with the rift having opened and closed multiple times over tens of thousands of years, suggesting it may be a recurring phenomenon rather than a singular event. Whether it represents a natural flaw in dimensional topology or the consequence of some unimaginable act of engineering is a question that has consumed careers without yielding answers.

The Schism is currently classified as an exclusion zone with a mandatory 5,000-kilometer standoff distance, though this margin grows less comfortable with each passing decade. A consortium of research institutions maintains a distant observation platform that continuously monitors the rift's expansion rate and catalogs the alien transmissions that leak from its edges. The central question — what lies on the other side, and whether it is aware of us — remains unanswered, and for many, that uncertainty is the most dangerous thing about the Nightfall Schism.
